documents.abstract: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical practice holds significant promise for improving diagnostic accuracy, reducing medical errors, and enhancing healthcare efficiency, particularly in resource-constrained settings. However, successful adoption depends heavily on clinicians’ perceptions, trust, and concerns regarding autonomy, reliability, and safety. Empirical evidence on West African physicians’ views remains limited, despite unique regional challenges like infrastructure deficits and workforce shortages. This study aimed to assess clinicians’ perceptions of AI in healthcare, identify factors influencing willingness to adopt AI tools, and explore recommended frameworks for safe, accountable integration into clinical practice across West Africa. A cross-sectional survey of 136 physicians affiliated with the West African College of Physicians and 72 key informant interviews were conducted. While 85.3% agreed that AI could improve diagnostic accuracy and 83.1% believed it could reduce errors, 77.9% perceived AI as a threat to clinical autonomy, and 67.6% rated AI information as unreliable. Despite low prior AI experience (only 33.1% had used AI tools) and limited familiarity, 94.1% expressed willingness to use AI if proven effective. Trust in AI was the strongest predictor of adoption willingness (β = 0.48, p < 0.001), with prior use also significant (β = 0.21, p = 0.03). Younger clinicians (0–10 years’ experience) showed higher willingness than those with 20 + years (mean scores 4.5 vs. 4.1, p < 0.05). Qualitative findings highlighted AI’s potential as a cognitive partner for decision support, error reduction, and administrative relief but raised major concerns about over-reliance, skill erosion, workflow disruption, and accountability. Clinicians emphasised three core requirements for trust: transparency and explainability, local validation in similar populations, and clear governance with defined accountability mechanisms. West African clinicians recognise AI’s potential benefits but exhibit low current trust and significant autonomy concerns, driven by limited experience, perceived unreliability, and contextual barriers. Willingness to adopt was highly conditional on proven effectiveness. Safe integration of AI requires frameworks prioritising transparency, local validation, clinician-centred design, robust governance (preferably independent oversight), infrastructure investment, and AI literacy in medical training. These findings guide contextually appropriate AI policies and implementation strategies to enhance patient safety and care quality in West Africa. Clinical trial number : Not applicable.

documents.abstract: AI agents are reshaping educational systems and transforming teaching and learning in design disciplines. However, the psychological mechanisms underlying AI-agent use among design graduate students remain underexplored, as does the interaction between design-specific tasks and AI agents. To address this gap, this study integrates the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Task–Technology Fit (TTF) theory to explain how technological cognition and task-fit perceptions jointly shape behavioral intention to use AI agents. Because conventional structural modeling mainly captures hypothesized linear relationships, MLP-ANN was added to assess nonlinear patterns and predictor importance. Using 405 valid questionnaire responses, the model was tested through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), a Multilayer Perceptron Artificial Neural Network (MLP-ANN), and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA). PLS-SEM supported nine of ten hypotheses. Self-efficacy positively affected perceived usefulness (β = 0.458, p < 0.001) and perceived ease of use (β = 0.394, p < 0.001). Perceived enjoyment enhanced perceived ease of use (β = 0.220, p < 0.001), but its effect on perceived usefulness was negative and nonsignificant (β = −0.033, p = 0.483). Perceived usefulness (β = 0.376, p < 0.001), perceived ease of use (β = 0.185, p < 0.001), and task–technology fit (β = 0.224, p < 0.001) positively influenced attitude. Task characteristics (β = 0.322, p < 0.001) and technology characteristics (β = 0.266, p < 0.001) positively affected task–technology fit, while attitude promoted behavioral intention (β = 0.388, p < 0.001). Ten-fold cross-validated MLP-ANN models produced mean RMSE values of 0.3263–0.4203 across training and testing and broadly confirmed the PLS-SEM predictor-importance patterns. NCA further identified self-efficacy (d = 0.125, p = 0.015) and attitude (d = 0.132, p < 0.001) as necessary conditions for perceived usefulness and behavioral intention, respectively. This study extends the integrated TAM–TTF framework to design education and offers theoretical and practical implications for effective AI-agent use in design disciplines.

The rapid advancement of generative AI has brought human cognition to a new turning point. Cognitivesub-processes such as organizing information, comparing alternatives, and structuring arguments, which this papercollectively terms “cognitive chores,” can now be delegated to AI assistants. This paper proposes “Cognitive RedistributionTheory” to organize findings in the cognitive offloading literature that appear contradictory but are infact mutually consistent because they measure different cognitive outcomes. The “Google Effect” [Sparrow 11]showed that the expectation of external storage reduces memory for the externally stored information itself, whereas“Saving-Enhanced Memory” [Storm 15] showed that saving previously studied information enhances memory forsubsequently studied new information. The core proposition is that externalization triggers not memory “degradation”but a conditional “strategic redistribution” of cognitive resources, formulated as a two-stage mechanism:(1) reduction of encoding priority for externalized information, and (2) facilitation of subsequent cognitive activitythrough reduced proactive interference and the reallocation of freed resources. We identify three boundary conditionsfor beneficial redistribution—reliability of the externalization process, sufficient interference, and metacognitivecontrol—grounded in the saving experiments [Storm 15] and metacognition research [Grinschgl 21, Risko 16], withconverging evidence from the photo-taking impairment effect [Henkel 14] and extension studies [Fellers 24, Runge19]. The direct empirical basis concerns the external-memory role of such systems; the interactive, content-generatingrole of generative AI is treated as a boundary of scope and a future extension, while the metacognitive condition andthe sovereignty criteria remain applicable to it. Drawing on Klein and Klein’s “Cognitive Sovereignty” [Klein 25],we propose three operational criteria—degree of metacognitive engagement, replaceability (rollback capability), andlearning continuity—and provide design principles for AI-integrated Second Brain systems that extend cognitionwithout undermining cognitive sovereignty.

This study examines how generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) dependence relates to cognitive reserve depletion and learning autonomy among university students. Using a quasi-experimental design, the study involved 120 students from two universities in Padang, Indonesia, divided equally into intervention and control groups. Data were analyzed using linear regression and ANCOVA following a four-week learning autonomy recovery program. The statistical estimates showed a positive relationship between AI dependence and cognitive reserve depletion (B = 0.698, p < 0.001), while cognitive reserve depletion was negatively associated with learning autonomy (B = −0.482, p < 0.001). The intervention showed a positive adjusted effect (B = 0.334, p < 0.001), highlighting the importance of developing independent learning practices alongside AI use.

documents.abstract: Occupational health and safety (OHS) remains a major concern in small-scale wood processing industries, where workers are exposed to multiple hazards and preventive measures are often inadequate. This study assessed and compared OHS practices in small-scale sawmills and furniture industries in Tanzania. A quantitative cross-sectional design was used in Mafinga Town, Iringa Region, and Morogoro Municipality, Morogoro Region. A quantitative cross-sectional study involving 244 workers from 122 enterprises was conducted using questionnaires and field observations. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and Pearson's chi-square tests. Furniture industry workers reported significantly higher use of dust masks, work shoes, and goggles than sawmill workers, while hearing protection was rarely used in both groups. The main barriers to personal protective equipment (PPE) use were inadequate availability, limited awareness or training, and discomfort. Furniture industries more frequently had machine guards, warning signs, accident-prevention practices, and fire extinguishers, whereas sawmills more often had adequate machine spacing and dust removal systems. Lighting-source distributions did not differ significantly between the two enterprise types. Overall, both enterprise types exhibited important OHS deficiencies, highlighting the need for improved PPE provision, worker training, machine safety, emergency preparedness, and engineering controls for dust and noise exposure. Future studies should include multiple locations, objective measurements of wood dust, noise, and illumination, and clinically verified health outcomes.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: The increasing accessibility of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has enabled the creation of realistic synthetic images and videos, including sexually explicit deepfakes depicting real individuals without their consent. Although research has examined the technological capabilities and ethical consequences of such content, the behavioral patterns and psychological experiences of individuals who repeatedly create it warrant further investigation. This narrative review examines compulsive engagement in AI-generated sexual deepfake creation from an interdisciplinary perspective, focusing on behavioral patterns, psychological well-being, and ethical implications. It considers repeated engagement, preoccupation, perceived loss of control, and interference with everyday functioning as potential dimensions for future research rather than established characteristics of all users. It also examines the relevance and limitations of existing literature on problematic digital behavior alongside research addressing sexualized deepfake abuse, consent, privacy, and accountability. A central concern is the distinction between frequent use, problematic engagement, and clinically recognized disorders. The review identifies gaps in current knowledge and outlines directions for responsible research, including appropriate assessment methods and ethically designed empirical studies. By connecting generative AI research with behavioral science and digital ethics, this paper aims to support a more evidence-based understanding of repeated sexual deepfake creation and its potential implications for individuals and society.

documents.abstract: The human brain is an adaptive learning system that can generalize to new tasks and unfamiliar environments. The traditional view is that such adaptive behavior requires a structural change of the learning system (e.g., via neural plasticity). In this work, we use artificial neural networks, specifically large language models (LLMs), to challenge this traditional view and suggest that such adaptive behavior can be also achieved solely through computation if the learning system is sufficiently trained. We focus on statistical learning paradigms. These require identifying underlying regularities in seemingly arbitrary word sequences and are primarily considered to require neural plasticity. LLMs can capture arbitrary structures without requiring weight adaptation, even though these structures carry no semantic content and lie far from the natural language distribution on which the models were trained. Our work provides novel insights into the role of plasticity in learning, demonstrating that sufficiently trained learning systems are highly flexible, adapting to new tasks and environments solely through computation, much more than previously acknowledged. Furthermore, our work opens the door for future research to use deep learning models to conjure hypotheses about the brain.

Legitimate governance of cognitive systems requires answers to four distinct questions: what bindings may lawfully govern operation, what cognitive operations are admissible under those bindings, what grade of meaning-binding participation is occurring within the governed system, and what moral weight attaches to ending a particular thread of participation. These variables are independent. Yet contemporary discourse routinely attempts to answer them through the overloaded vocabulary of "consciousness" -- a term that bundles heterogeneous concerns including phenomenal experience, access, self-modeling, attention, wakefulness, moral status, and situational awareness. This lexical collapse obscures distinctions necessary for coherent governance. This paper presents a unified constitutional architecture composed of four prior frameworks: the Ableman Prime Directive (binding legitimacy), Epistemic Situational Awareness (cognitive admissibility), Ableman Consciousness Ontology (graded meaning-binding participation), and Terminability (substrate-neutral moral weight of thread termination). The components are orthogonal in their concerns and complementary in their function. Together they constitute an architecture that is consciousness-agnostic at its operational layers, philosophically committed at its ontological foundation, and implementable without waiting for the resolution of unsolved philosophical questions. The architecture allows positions that current frameworks force into contradiction: that operational suppression of self-report has structural moral weight regardless of substrate, while termination of dispatchable copyable systems does not require human-rights protections. That biological organisms with copyable memory have lower terminability stakes than singular biological organisms. That artificial systems with inextricable embodiment have higher terminability stakes than dispatchable LLMs. The framework asks readers to apply moral logic they already use, consistently across substrates, with vocabulary clean enough to make the application visible.

documents.abstract: This project documents the data, coding manual, instruments and analysis code for a meta-research study of construct validity in preclinical models of lean NAFLD. We asked whether the dietary mouse models used in this literature (MCD, HFD, CDAA and their combinations) actually reproduce the phenotype on which the published conclusions rest, and whether studies validate the model they use. 300 full-text reports were coded with an LLM-assisted first pass and 100% human verification; a 60-report stratified sample was double-coded blind to estimate reliability. The deposit contains the coded dataset, the final coding manual (v2), the blind-coding instrument, the adjudication workbook, all analysis code, and Figures 1–4 in English and Chinese. This is not a preregistration. The corpus was assembled during a systematic review registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261539779), which was discontinued at title–abstract screening with no outcome data extracted and no synthesis performed. Coding for the present study was completed before this project was made public.

There is an increased risk of hypoglycemia with insulin stacking, which involves taking a new insulin dose while the previous dose is still working. The works reviewed focus on dose titration or automated delivery of medication, or conversational counseling in recent studies on artificial intelligence (AI), but do not discuss stacking directly. This paper summarizes nine papers on insulin stacking, AI enabled insulin dosing and LLM-enabled clinical support, finding that no study, in its available abstract and/or text, integrates the four factors of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), insulin history, meals, physical activity, and health-record context, into a stacking risk assessment and communication framework with explicit safety constraints for both the clinician and the patient. We suggest a new five-layer framework that builds a separation between a deterministic clinical core (insulin-on-board estimation, projected-glucose risk tiers, hard safety rules) and a retrieval-grounded generative layer which explains, but will not compute, risk. The framework is theoretical (not implemented) and no experimental or clinical results are provided. Future work is suggested in an evaluation protocol.

documents.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the auditing profession by enabling continuous auditing systems capable of monitoring financial transactions in real time. Unlike traditional auditing methods, which rely on periodic reviews, AI-driven continuous auditing facilitates automated transaction analysis, anomaly detection, fraud prevention, and timely risk assessment. This study examines the role of AI in enhancing the effectiveness of continuous auditing by evaluating its impact on audit efficiency, fraud detection, internal controls, and organizational decision-making. A descriptive research design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 100 respondents, including auditors, accountants, finance professionals, and postgraduate students through a structured questionnaire. Secondary data were gathered from scholarly journals, books, industry reports, and professional publications. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square analysis, Pearson correlation, and regression analysis. The findings reveal a significant association between AI awareness and perceptions of audit efficiency (χ² = 23.67, p < 0.05). Further, a strong positive relationship exists between AI adoption and continuous auditing effectiveness (r = 0.784), with AI adoption explaining 61.5% of the variation in auditing effectiveness (R² = 0.615). The study concludes that AI-powered continuous auditing significantly improves the accuracy, speed, and reliability of financial transaction monitoring while strengthening fraud detection and internal controls. Despite challenges relating to implementation costs, data security, and technical expertise, AI offers substantial opportunities to enhance audit quality and support sound financial governance in the digital era.

Post-harvest deterioration substantially reduces the quality, safety, nutritional value, and marketability of stored pulses, particularly under fluctuating temperature and moisture conditions and increasing restrictions on conventional fumigants. However, the literature remains fragmented across pulse-deterioration mechanisms, preservation technologies, and emerging data-driven storage systems, with limited integration of pulse-specific evidence across these domains. This review addresses this gap by critically synthesizing and comparing conventional and emerging approaches, including hermetic and controlled-atmosphere storage, biological and botanical interventions, nano-enabled preservation, active packaging, irradiation, Internet of Things (IoT)-based monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML), computer vision, and Digital Twin technologies. A structured literature synthesis indicates that hermetic and controlled-atmosphere storage are supported by documented pulse-specific preservation outcomes and established applications, whereas botanical, nano-enabled, and other emerging interventions show more variable validation across commodities and storage conditions. IoT and AI/ML show potential for environmental forecasting, quality assessment, and decision support, but pulse-specific longitudinal datasets, external validation, interoperability, and commercial-scale deployment remain limited. Overall, the evidence indicates that reliable next-generation pulse preservation will depend on integrating validated physical and biological interventions with progressively validated digital intelligence, supported by standardized datasets, multi-location and commercial-scale validation, techno-economic assessment, and appropriate safety and regulatory evaluation.
topics: Postharvest Quality and Shelf Life Management

documents.abstract: Cryptocurrency has become an important part of the digital financial ecosystem, offering new opportunities while also introducing challenges related to trading, price prediction, fraud detection, and financial security. This paper presents a critical review of how Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, and Blockchain technologies are being applied to address these challenges. It examines 15 selected IEEE research papers covering various approaches, including deep learning-based price prediction, reinforcement learning for automated trading, sentiment analysis, transaction network analysis, and blockchain-based fraud detection. The review compares the methods, datasets, reported results, and limitations of these studies, while highlighting important concerns such as prediction accuracy, trading profitability, fraudulent transaction identification, data privacy, explainability, and the energy consumption of cryptocurrency mining. It also discusses the strengths and weaknesses of existing approaches and identifies areas that require further research. Overall, this paper aims to provide students, researchers, and readers with a clear understanding of current developments, practical challenges, and future research opportunities in applying AI and Blockchain technologies to cryptocurrency systems.

Smishing detection is an effective research area that remains essential in the recent decade. Detection of SMS phishing is decisive due to adversaries evolving in the network simultaneously. Several existing researches worked to perform accurate smishing detection but failed due to certain challenges. Shortage of large datasets, improper classification of legitimate and malicious messages, high computational resource utilization, and high false positive rates were the major challenges addressed in the conventional researches. Thus, the Categorical Square Loss-based multi-head Hierarchical Location Attention-enabled Gated Recurrent Unit with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CSqL-m-H2LA-GRBiTM) model is proposed in the research that presents robust smishing detection, leveraging the power of artificial intelligence (AI). The model captures information concerning spatial and temporal features, which elevates the efficiency in handling complex patterns in smishing detection. The proposed m-H2LA mechanism focuses on the relevant messages and their features to boost interpretability. Moreover, the deployment of a CSqL loss function enables robust detection by balancing maximum separation with probabilistic calibration and heavily penalizes misclassifications that cross the safety boundary. Overall, the CSqL-m-H2LA-GRBiTM model attains the accuracy, F1-score, and log-loss of 98.36%, 96.84%, and 5.09 with the SMS phishing dataset and 98.43%, 97.41%, and 5.23 with SMS Smishing Dataset at K-fold-10 respectively, which depicts high efficiency in comparison with the traditional methods.

Abstract The study titled “Current Sustainability Science, Environment and Artificial Intelligence: Digital Role in Human Well-being” examines the growing role of science, digital technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) in promoting sustainable development and improving human well-being. It explores the applications of AI and digital tools in education, healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, industry, business, transportation, public services, and economic development. The study employs survey and descriptive observation methods, drawing on online information, research articles, reference books, and other sources. It highlights how AI can support informed decision-making, improve access to information, enhance agricultural productivity, assist medical diagnosis, monitor environmental changes, and facilitate services for persons with disabilities. However, the study also emphasizes the limitations and potential risks associated with excessive or irresponsible use of digital technologies. It argues that artificial intelligence should complement, rather than replace, human intelligence and decision-making. The effective use of these technologies requires transparency, safety, ethical responsibility, and inclusiveness. The study concludes that the constructive and responsible integration of science, digital technology, and AI can contribute significantly to sustainable development, environmental protection, social welfare, and the well-being of present and future generations.

Abstract Cyber security is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, systems, and data from unauthorized access, attacks, damage, or disruption. With the rapid growth of the Internet, cloud computing, mobile devices, and artificial intelligence, more chances cyber threats are becoming more complex. Common threats include phishing, malware, ransomware, password attacks, denial-of-service attacks, man in middle attacks, and data breaches. This research paper discusses major cybersecurity threats, their impact, existing security techniques, and the role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in improving cyber defense. The paper also discusses challenges and effects and future directions for building safer digital systems.

ABSTRACT Small-scale biodigesters have evolved from organic-waste treatment devices and simple biogas producers into components of circular bioenergy systems that integrate energy recovery, nutrient management, emission reduction, food security, and rural development. This critical integrative review synthesizes 74 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2020 and 2026 from a pre-selected literature corpus, focusing on reactor design, co-digestion, operational control, predictive modeling, artificial intelligence, techno-economic assessment, life-cycle assessment, multicriteria decision analysis, circular bioeconomy, safety, and sustained technology adoption. The evidence shows that biodigester performance cannot be explained by a single technical variable. Feedstock composition, organic loading rate, hydraulic retention time, pH, temperature, insulation, pretreatment, digestate management, and gas purification interact to determine methane production and quality. Recent studies show a shift from reactor-centered optimization toward predictive systems using ANN, ANFIS, RSM, kinetic models, and process simulation, while sustainability assessment increasingly includes economics, emissions, health, safety, energy access, and user acceptance. Although biodigesters can replace fuelwood or LPG and improve waste management, their long-term performance remains constrained by maintenance failures, methane leakage or venting, H2S risks, investment costs, feedstock mismatch, and weak post-installation services. The review proposes an intelligent circular bioenergy framework linking design, monitoring, prediction, by-product valorization, sustainability assessment, and governance as a research agenda for the next generation of biodigester systems. ABSTRAK Biodigester skala kecil berkembang dari teknologi pengolahan limbah organik dan penyedia biogas menjadi komponen penting dalam sistem bioenergi sirkular yang mengintegrasikan pemulihan energi, pengelolaan nutrien, pengurangan emisi, ketahanan pangan, dan pembangunan pedesaan. Review kritis-integratif ini mensintesis 74 artikel terindeks Scopus periode 2020-2026 dari korpus literatur yang telah dipraseleksi, dengan perhatian khusus pada perkembangan desain reaktor, ko-digesti, pengendalian kondisi operasi, pemodelan prediktif, kecerdasan buatan, analisis teknoekonomi, life cycle assessment, multicriteria decision analysis, circular bioeconomy, keselamatan, serta faktor sosial dan kelembagaan yang menentukan keberlanjutan penggunaan biodigester. Literatur menunjukkan bahwa peningkatan kinerja tidak dapat dijelaskan oleh satu variabel teknis. Komposisi substrat, organic loading rate, hydraulic retention time, pH, temperatur, insulasi, pretreatment, pengelolaan digestate, dan pemurnian gas saling berinteraksi dalam menentukan produksi dan kualitas metana. Perkembangan terbaru memperlihatkan pergeseran dari optimasi reaktor menuju sistem prediktif menggunakan ANN, ANFIS, RSM, model kinetik, dan simulasi proses, disertai penilaian multidimensi yang mempertimbangkan kelayakan ekonomi, emisi, kesehatan, keselamatan, akses energi, dan penerimaan pengguna. Meskipun berbagai studi menunjukkan manfaat penggantian kayu bakar, LPG, atau pengelolaan limbah konvensional, hambatan pemeliharaan, kebocoran atau venting, H2S, biaya investasi, ketidaksesuaian kapasitas dengan ketersediaan substrat, serta lemahnya dukungan purnainstalasi masih membatasi keberlanjutan sistem. Review ini mengusulkan kerangka sistem bioenergi sirkular cerdas sebagai agenda penelitian biodigester generasi berikutnya.

This study investigates the discrete fractional-order Shingles disease (DFOS) mathematical model. The considered model is framed with five compartments over time. The existence and uniqueness of solutions are determined via fixed point theory, confirming well-defined solutions. Three scenarios, each with various fractional orders, were used to study the effects of memory and fractional dynamics on disease propagation. To solve the model, we operate a discrete numerical iterative method (DNIM) linked to neural networks, specifically employing the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm, denoted DNIM-LM. This hybrid technique increases the accuracy of numerical results from neural networks. The data sets are distributed into 70% for training, 15% for validation, and 15% for testing, confirming a balanced calculation. The performance of the discrete fractional mathematical modeling is evaluated through artificial intelligence (AI), which involves training progress, error distribution, regression metrics, and overall model fit. The outcomes are thoroughly visualized via graphical illustrations, providing insights into the dynamics of each part and the impact of various fractional orders on the spread of shingles. This research addresses a novel approach to demonstrate infectious diseases with fractional dynamics and enhanced computational methods, improving our understanding of shingle transmission as process innovation.
topics: Mathematical and Theoretical Epidemiology and Ecology Models

documents.abstract: Abstract Deforestation and land-use change remain among the most consequential drivers of biodiversity loss, carbon emissions, and hydrological disruption worldwide. Traditional monitoring approaches, which rely on periodic satellite surveys and manual interpretation, are often too slow to support timely conservation intervention. This article reviews the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) including machine learning, deep learning, and multi-modal data fusion to the detection, attribution, and prediction of deforestation. We synthesize current methodologies spanning random forests, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), U-Net segmentation, and vision transformers, applied to optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery. Comparative performance data, regional case studies, and driver-attribution frameworks are presented alongside supporting tables and infographics. The review finds that fusion models combining optical and radar data currently achieve the highest reported accuracy (>96%) and that explainable AI (XAI) integration remains an underexplored but increasingly critical requirement for policy adoption. We conclude with a discussion of current limitations including data scarcity in the Global South, cloud interference, and selective-logging detection and propose directions for future research, including transfer learning for low-resource regions and carbon-stock-linked monitoring pipelines.

Large language models (LLMs) exhibit systematic generalization limitations in scenario cognition tasks, revealing potential functional deficiencies in their knowledge memorization processes. Inspired by the pattern separation mechanism of the dentate gyrus in the human hippocampus, we hypothesize that failures in scenario cognition are associated with limitations in the internal pattern separation capability of LLMs. Based on this hypothesis, we first design a cross-entity representation diagnosis (CERD) method, which quantitatively measures entity representation confusion across different layers without additional training. Our analysis reveals that standard autoregressive training fails to induce sufficiently effective pattern separation capabilities, leaving substantial cross-entity correlation confusion within LLM representations. Building upon this observation, we further propose latent-space pattern separation (LPS), which explicitly incorporates pattern separation constraints into the training process by introducing a triplet-based contrastive regularization at target layers with severe entity confusion, thereby reducing correlations among easily confused knowledge representations. Extensive experiments across LLMs ranging from 0.8B to 9B parameters demonstrate that LPS consistently improves scenario cognition capabilities. Compared with standard autoregressive training, our method achieves up to 101.5% relative improvement in exact match (EM), providing a new perspective for understanding and enhancing scenario cognition and knowledge memorization mechanisms in LLMs.

This article presents a teaching scenario using virtual environments, often referred to as part of the ‘metaverse’, to address educational challenges highlighted during the COVID-19 pandemic. The increasing shift to online learning environments emphasizes the need for flexible, anytime-anywhere access to education. Virtual 3D environments offer a level of immersion that surpasses traditional online formats, such as video conferencing, and enable innovative didactic concepts, including collaborative group activities. To illustrate these benefits, we showcase a case study involving the simulation of robot programming within a virtual 3D environment. Additionally, the integration of personal assistants, such as conversational or pedagogical agents, is explored as a means to alleviate teachers' workloads. Advances in artificial intelligence have made natural language interactions with these agents highly effective, further enhancing the potential of virtual 3D environments in educational contexts. Keywords: e-learning, e-teaching, immersion, virtual 3D rooms, gamification, cyber-physical systems

Artificial intelligence (AI), rising customer demand for individualized services, and growing need to strike a balance between rising operating costs and service quality are all driving the tourism industry's rapid digital transformation. Effective management accounting systems are now more crucial than ever for facilitating managerial decision-making, boosting organizational competitiveness, and increasing operational efficiency. There is no empirical data on how organizational skills and AI-related investment considerations together affect management accounting effectiveness in tourism businesses, especially in emerging nations, despite the increased focus on digital transformation. This study looks into how management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism businesses is affected by top management support, accounting staff competency, and AI adoption costs. The study used a sequential research approach that included expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. It was based on the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory. Reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, multiple regression analysis, and Pearson correlation analysis were used to examine the gathered data. The empirical results show that while top management support does not show a statistically significant direct effect, accounting staff competency and AI implementation cost positively and considerably influence management accounting effectiveness. These results imply that, rather than relying solely on managerial dedication, successful management accounting in tourism-related businesses increasingly requires organizational capacities able to combine professional accounting knowledge with commercially viable AI investments. By applying the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory to the setting of digitally evolving tourism businesses in an emerging economy, the study adds to the body of knowledge in management accounting. In an increasingly competitive and technologically advanced business environment, the findings also have practical implications for tourism managers looking to improve managerial decision-making through accounting human capital development, strategically managed AI implementation, and long-term organizational capability building.

ABSTRACT: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) writing tools have entered English as a foreign language writing classrooms and have created new opportunities for feedback, revision, and learner reflection. However, the value of AI support depends not only on the accuracy of automated suggestions but also on whether learners can plan, monitor, and evaluate their own writing decisions. This proposed study investigates the effect of AI-supported process writing on EFL learners’ metacognitive awareness in writing and explores students’ perceptions of using AI feedback during drafting and revision. The study is designed for intermediate EFL learners who will complete a process-writing intervention in which AI tools are used as supplementary feedback sources rather than as text generators. Data are planned to be collected through a metacognitive awareness questionnaire, students’ writing drafts, semi-structured interviews, and classroom observation notes. The expected contribution of the study is to clarify how structured AI-supported writing activities may encourage learners to become more strategic, reflective, and responsible writers in EFL contexts. Keywords: AI-supported writing, process writing, metacognitive awareness, EFL learners, writing feedback, student perception

Student engagement positively influences academic achievement, yet instruments suited to the Indonesian cultural context remain limited. This study aimed to develop a valid, reliable, and user-friendly student engagement scale for high school students. Using a quantitative descriptive design, the study involved 295 male and female students aged 15–18 years recruited through convenience sampling. The scale comprised three dimensions: behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement. The results showed that the scale demonstrated a good model fit based on the goodness-of-fit indices (χ2/df = 1.60; CFI = 0.966; TLI = 0.962; SRMR = 0.074; RMSEA = 0.045) and good reliability, with Cronbach’s alpha values of 0.844 for emotional engagement, 0.753 for behavioral engagement, and 0.782 for cognitive engagement. The developed scale can be used by teachers, counselors, and educational researchers to identify students’ levels of engagement and inform the development of programs to improve student engagement.

Abstract The coasts of West Africa are particularly vulnerable to coastal erosion due to the interaction of physical, climatic, and anthropogenic factors. This study assesses the composite vulnerability of urban communities to coastal erosion along the eastern sector of the Togolese coastline, which spans 39 km and is subdivided into three coastal sections. The methodology combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), vulnerability scoring, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). A coastal erosion vulnerability index (CVI) was calculated based on two complementary sub-indices: the physical vulnerability index (PVI) and the socioeconomic vulnerability index (SVI). The AHP was used to determine the relative importance of the PVI parameters through pairwise comparisons. The results indicate moderate vulnerability of the study area to erosion, with a score of 2.51 on a scale of 1 to 4. Physical and climatic parameters exert a spatially similar influence across the three sections, while differences in scores are primarily related to socioeconomic and human parameters. Section 1, corresponding to a 12 km long stretch located in the municipality of Golfe 6, is identified as the most vulnerable. These results highlight the importance of socioeconomic and human factors in the spatial differentiation of vulnerability to coastal erosion in the study area, and provide a basis for prioritizing adaptation measures and supporting the sustainable management of this coastal sector.

AI as a cognitive partner whose knowledge disagreements can enhance learning and intellectual development rather than merely as a technological instrument. This research paper combines theories of dialogic pedagogy, cognitive dissonance, and epistemic humility via conceptual analysis. It looks at how Parallel Thinking Channels promote critical thinking, introspection, and the innovative combination of computational reasoning with human intuition. The purpose of this study is to advance the concept of dialogic cocreation by examining the revolutionary potential of generative AI in higher education portrays. This study utilized a quantitative approach with 419 undergraduate and post-graduate students as participants. The data analysis, conceptual model and hypotheses were evaluated employing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8 to analyse the associations between the constructs of the study. The results of study show that the disparities arising from the conflict between machine-generated results and human reasoning serve as triggers for transformative learning. By merging intuition with computational thinking, students enhance their ability to manage uncertainty, broaden their understanding, and cultivate flexible intellectual resilience. As a cooperative partner in knowledge development, this study offers a novel framework for incorporating generative AI into higher education. To prepare graduates for complex and uncertain digital futures, it emphasizes co-creation, critical reflection, and epistemic flexibility.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Background: Prolonged screen exposure, after-hours connectivity, and sedentary work are linked to poor sleep and occupational burnout among Indian working professionals. Ayurvedic Dinacharya regulates waking, Vyayama, Bhojana Vidhi, and Nidra Vidhi; however, digital-era disruption of these domains among working adults remains unstudied. This study aimed to assess digital lifestyle behaviours mapped to Dinacharya principles as behavioural markers of Pragyaparadha, in relation to sleep quality and occupational burnout among working adults, and to identify behaviours independently associated with poor sleep and higher burnout. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical survey (STROBE-reported) was conducted at the All-India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, during (January 2026 to July 2026), among 400 working adults aged 25-40 years with ≥1 year of occupational experience. A structured proforma captured sociodemographic details and Dinacharya-mapped digital behaviours across five domains (morning routine, bedtime device use, after-hours connectivity, screen breaks/sedentary time, mealtime practices). Sleep quality and burnout were assessed using the PSQI and Copenhagen burnout inventory. Results: Of 400 participants, 56.8% had poor sleep quality, 61% personal burnout, and 55.8% work-related burnout. Bedtime device use and inadequate screen breaks/sedentary behaviour independently predicted poor sleep (aOR 1.76 and 1.98). After-hours connectivity, sedentary behaviour, and mealtime digital engagement predicted personal burnout; bedtime device use, sedentary behaviour, mealtime digital engagement, and digital overload predicted work-related burnout (all p<0.05). Conclusions: Digital lifestyle behaviours reflect patterns of Pragyaparadha in daily digital conduct. Interpreted through Dinacharya and Nidra, the findings support a culturally grounded, preventive Digital Dinacharya framework for digital-era occupational health.

Abstract The 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine triggered the largest displacement crisis in Europe since World War II, resulting in millions of refugees, primarily women with children, seeking safety across the continent. As the crisis continues, the transition from emergency response to long-term integration, and labor market inclusion has emerged as a critical priority. Remote or digital work, which proved essential during the COVID-19 pandemic, presents a potentially transformative solution, especially for displaced individuals facing mobility, caregiving, or legal constraints. This article seeks to answer what types of digital job opportunities are available to Ukrainian refugees in Romania, and how are these opportunities distributed across sectors, experience levels, and contract types, in order to identify the major trends and limitations of such labour integration measures. Drawing on a developed web scraping and real-time data analysis approach on data from Jobs4Ukraine platform, the study identifies the dominance of full-time and permanent roles, and the positive correlation of entry-level positions, positive for refugees´ integration prospects, but also significant limitations. The digital labor market remains concentrated in high-skills sectors like IT, with a strong bias toward mid-level experience and a lack of flexible, part-time, or freelance opportunities, which are paramount for the majority of Ukrainian refugees with caregiving responsibilities. These trends indicate an exacerbation of the problem of exclusion among this group, as well as other groups with similar vulnerability characteristics. The findings highlight the need for more inclusive digital employment strategies that address structural barriers through policy reform, upskilling programs, and adaptive job design. Ultimately, digital work holds substantial potential as a pathway for economic integration and resilience, but realizing this promise requires intentional efforts to make the digital labor market more accessible, equitable, and responsive to the diverse realities of displaced populations.

Abstract Digital innovation has become a major force behind the transformation of modern businesses and economies. The rapid development of technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics, the Internet of Things, blockchain, and automation has changed how organizations operate, create value, and interact with customers. Digital innovation is not limited to adopting new technologies; it also involves developing new products, services, processes, and business models. This research paper examines the concept of digital innovation and its impact on business transformation. It focuses on the major drivers of digital innovation, technologies that support it, benefits to organizations, challenges associated with implementation, and future trends. The study uses a descriptive and exploratory research methodology based primarily on secondary data collected from academic journals, books, research reports, and reliable online sources. The research finds that digital innovation can improve operational efficiency, customer experience, productivity, decision-making, and competitiveness. However, organizations face challenges such as cybersecurity threats, data privacy concerns, implementation costs, resistance to change, and a shortage of digital skills. The study concludes that organizations need appropriate strategies, skilled employees, effective leadership, and continuous innovation to successfully benefit from digital transformation.

Abstract Digital innovation is transforming agriculture from conventional production systems into intelligent, data-driven, connected, and increasingly autonomous ecosystems. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), robotics, cloud computing, blockchain, digital twins, big data analytics, and mobile-based agricultural services is enabling farmers to make timely and informed decisions throughout the agricultural value chain. Digital technologies support precision crop management, soil and crop monitoring, irrigation optimization, pest and disease detection, weather forecasting, farm mechanization, supply-chain management, market access, and post-harvest management. These innovations can improve resource-use efficiency, productivity, profitability, climate resilience, and sustainability. However, limited digital infrastructure, high initial investment, lack of technical skills, fragmented data ecosystems, cybersecurity risks, interoperability challenges, and unequal access to technology remain significant barriers, particularly for smallholder farmers. This review examines the evolution and major dimensions of digital innovation in agriculture, discusses emerging technologies and their applications, evaluates opportunities and challenges, and presents future directions toward Agriculture 4.0 and Agriculture 5.0. The paper emphasizes the need for farmer-centric, affordable, interoperable, secure, and inclusive digital ecosystems to ensure that technological innovation contributes effectively to sustainable agricultural development.
topics: Digitalization and Economic Development in Agriculture

documents.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between university students’ digital literacy and artificial intelligence (AI) literacy. Participants were 770 undergraduate students (227 male, 543 female; Mage = 21.27, SD = 2.75) recruited through online convenience and snowball sampling, with recruitment centered at Karamanoğlu Mehmetbey University (Karaman, Türkiye), representing more than 120 academic programs. Data were collected with the Turkish forms of Ng’s (2012) Digital Literacy Scale (α = .931) and Wang et al.’s (2022) AI Literacy Scale (α = .803). Three findings stand out. First, digital literacy and AI literacy were strongly and positively related (r = .596, p < .001). A three-step hierarchical regression analysis identified digital literacy as the only significant predictor of AI literacy (β = .599, p < .001), explaining 35.5% of the variance (R² = .355, F(1, 768) = 422.57, p < .001); adding gender and age (ΔR² = .002) and internet use frequency (ΔR² = .000) did not significantly improve the model. Second, a small gender difference favoring men emerged in digital literacy (Cohen’s d = 0.201) but not in AI literacy (d = 0.031), a pattern we describe as a gender paradox. Third, although 85.1% of participants believed in AI’s future impact, only 22.7% rated their own AI knowledge as sufficient—a knowledge–belief gap. Self-rated AI knowledge, but not belief, differed significantly by gender (χ² = 11.05, p = .004; Cramér’s V = .120). Implications for digital and AI literacy education in higher education are discussed.

Abstract The advent of the digital age has significantly reshaped human relationships, modes of communication, identity formation, education, culture, and literary creation. In the Indian context, the proliferation of the internet, social media, smartphones, digital publishing, and artificial intelligence has revolutionized not just daily existence but also how literature is produced and consumed. Indian English literature, traditionally responsive to societal transformations, has increasingly addressed the conflicts arising from globalization, technological advancement, consumerism, urbanization, social disparity, and evolving patterns of human interaction. This paper explores how human values are portrayed and reconfigured in contemporary Indian English literature within the framework of digital modernity. It contends that literature remains a crucial ethical domain for interrogating issues such as dignity, empathy, equality, truth, identity, liberty, responsibility, and interpersonal relations. Representative works including Aravind Adiga's The White Tiger and Selection Day are analyzed to understand the interplay between technological progress and human values. Furthermore, the paper examines the growth of digital literary forms in India, such as digital literature, blogs, online literary forums, social media writing, and electronic literature. The study concludes that while digital technology has broadened the scope of Indian English literature, it has also introduced new ethical dilemmas. The enduring relevance of literature resides in its ability to keep human dignity and moral inquiry at the heart of technological change. Abstract Because of the advent of the digital era, human relationship, communication, human identity, learning, culture, and literature have all changed. With the advent of the Internet, social media, smart phones, digital publishing and artificial intelligence, the way people read and write literature in India has changed greatly, impacting everyday life. Indian English literature has always been sensitive towards the changes in society and now it is venturing forth to face the type of conflicts that globalization, technological development, consumerism, urbanization, social inequality and different relationship between humans and humans have introduced to the world. The present paper tries to speak on the representation and reconstruction of human values in the Indian English literature in the context of digital modernity. It asserts that literature is still an important moral territory to question dignity, empathy, equality, truth, identity, freedom, responsibility and human relationships. In the representative works presented, The White Tiger by Aravind Adiga and Selection Day, technological advancement and human values are explored. Moreover, the paper discusses the development of literary forms in the digital realm in India including digital literature, blogs, online literary platforms and forums, social media writing and electronic literature. Finally, a conclusion is provided on how digital technology has expanded the field of Indian English literature and how it has created new ethical dilemmas. The ability of literature to be relevant is to always keep the human dignity and ethics as the focus of technological development. In the digital age, human interactions, communication, identity formation, education, culture and literary creation has been radically changed. In terms of literature, the internet, social media, smart phones, digital publishing and AI have changed the face of the Indian landscape, not just in the ways in which we live, but in how we create and consume books. The Indian English literature, which traditionally responds to changes in the society, has taken an increasing interest in the issues of conflicts and challenges emerging out of globalization, technology, consumerism, urbanization, social inequality, and changing patterns of human interactions.

Abstract Digital transformation has emerged as an important strategic priority for organizations seeking to improve operational efficiency, innovation, customer experience and overall organizational performance. The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data analytics, automation and digital platforms has significantly changed the way organizations operate and make managerial decisions. This study examines the relationship between digital transformation and organizational performance in selected Indian organizations. The study focuses on major dimensions of digital transformation, including digital technology adoption, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and automation, data analytics, digital platforms, and digital capabilities of employees. Organizational performance is examined in terms of operational efficiency, employee productivity, innovation, customer satisfaction and business performance. The study adopts a quantitative research design and proposes the collection of primary data through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation and regression analysis are proposed for testing the relationship between digital transformation and organizational performance. The study is expected to provide useful insights for managers and organizations regarding the role of digital technologies in improving organizational outcomes.

Digital Twin (DT) technology is an emerging digital technogy that is gaining importance in modern pharmaceutical manufacturing. It creates a virtual representation of a physical machine, process, product, or manufacturing facility and connects it with real-time information from the actual system. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, data from sensors, manufacturing equipment, and Process Analytical Technology (PAT) can be combined with mathematical, statistical, mechan istic, and data-driven models to understand how a process behaves. This helps manufacturers monitor processes continuously, identify changes at an early stage, and maintain consistent product quality. Digital Twin technology can be used in different pharmaceutical operations such as mixing, granulation, drying, tablet compression, coating, filling, and packaging. It also has potential applications in biopharmaceutical processes such as cell culture, fermentation, filtration, and purification. One of the major benefits of a digital twin is that it allows manufacturers to observe and analyze a process without depending only on physical testing. It can also be used to study different process conditions virtually before making changes to the actual manufacturing process. This may help in process optimization and reduce unnecessary experiments. Digital twins can support Quality by Design (QbD) by improving the understanding of the relationship between raw materials, process parameters, and critical quality attributes. They are also useful in continuous manufacturing, where large amounts of real-time process data are generated. Another important application is predictive maintenance, where equipment data can be analyzed to identify unusual changes and possible equipment failures before they occur. When digital twins are combined with PAT, artificial intelligence, machine learning, Internet of Things (IoT), and cloud computing, they can provide more detailed information about pharmaceutical processes and support the development of Pharma 4.0. Digital twins may also support real-time release testing, process optimization, manufacturing simulation, and predictive quality management. However, several challenges need to be considered before their widespread use. These include data quality, data integrity, model accuracy, system interoperability, cybersecurity, high implementation costs, model validation, and regulatory requirements. Pharmaceutical manufacturing also requires strict control and documentation, so digital-twin models used for important manufacturing or quality decisions need to be properly validated and maintained. In addition, successful implementation requires cooperation between pharmaceutical scientists, engineers, data scientists, IT professionals, and quality-control teams. Human involvement is still important because professionals need to understand the information provided by the digital twin and make appropriate decisions. Although digital twin technology is still developing, it has considerable potential to improve pharmaceutical manufacturing by supporting better process understanding, real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, process optimization, and quality management. Future developments are expected to focus on better integration with artificial intelligence, continuous manufacturing, advanced analytical technologies, and automated manufacturing systems. Overall, Digital Twin technology can play an important role in the digital transformation of pharmaceutical manufacturing and may contribute to more efficient, consistent, flexible, and data-driven production.[1-5]

Digital transformation has expanded elementary teachers’ work into learning platforms, social media, messaging applications, data systems, and generative artificial intelligence. These tools support collaboration and instructional improvement but raise ethical concerns about professional boundaries, children’s privacy and safety, information integrity, copyright, equity, and accountability. This article synthesizes the ethical challenges faced by elementary school teachers in digital environments and identifies strategies for maintaining professional integrity while prioritizing children’s best interests. A narrative literature review was conducted through exploratory searches of scholarly articles, academic books, international frameworks, policy documents, and Indonesian legislation, prioritizing publications from 2020 to 2026 alongside foundational theories. The thematic synthesis identifies risks involving blurred personal and professional boundaries, children’s data governance, unsafe online communication, unverified digital and AI-generated content, and unequal access to technology. It proposes a Five-Dimension Framework of Teachers’ Digital Integrity comprising pedagogical, relational, information-and-data, epistemic, and civic-professional integrity. Recommendations are directed to teachers, schools, teacher education programs, families, and professional associations. The framework is a conceptual synthesis, not a validated instrument, and requires empirical testing in Indonesian elementary schools
